verdict: McDonald's grew revenue 8% to $6.4B and operating income 8% to $2.8B as global comparable sales rose 3.4% — though the war in the Middle East held back its licensed markets.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago; +6% in constant currencies

segments.name: Franchised restaurants
segments.note: Rent and royalties paid by the local owners who run most McDonald's restaurants — the heart of the business model.

segments.note: Fees and other income beyond rent, royalties and restaurant sales.

opex.note: Head office, marketing support and running the global franchising machine — includes $91M of depreciation and amortization and $31M of other operating expense.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $360M on McDonald's debt, partly offset by $73M of net nonoperating income.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: McDonald's reports in tenths of a million; this page rounds to whole millions (reported operating income was $2,801.9M and net income $2,039.0M). Other revenues are shown as $63M rather than the rounded $64M so the three revenue lines tie exactly to the reported $6,406M total.

takeaways.title: Comparable sales stayed positive everywhere
takeaways.text: Global comparable sales rose 3.4% — U.S. +4.3% and International Operated Markets +4.4% — while International Developmental Licensed Markets managed only +0.7% as the war in the Middle East weighed on sales.

takeaways.title: Revenue and profit both grew 8%
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 8% to $6,406M and operating income 8% to $2,802M. For the full year, global comparable sales grew 9% — more than 30% above 2019 levels — and systemwide sales to loyalty members passed $20B.

takeaways.title: Charges trimmed EPS
takeaways.text: EPS rose 8% to $2.80 despite $138M of pre-tax charges — a $72M write-off of software no longer in use and $66M for the Accelerating the Arches restructuring. Excluding them, EPS was $2.95, up 14%.

oneTimers: Pre-tax charges of $138M ($0.15 per share): $72M to write off impaired software no longer in use, and $66M related to the Accelerating the Arches growth strategy, including restructuring for 'Accelerating the Organization,' the company's internal modernization program. Excluding them, EPS was $2.95.
